description: Source-controlled operational task list for CommonUnity. These are deliberately deferred until after the private beta ships. Read-only for now, surfaced in /admin. The shape (stable id, title, rationale, phase, status, completion_criteria) is designed to migrate into an editable admin table later without breaking the API.

phases.beta: Work that must exist before / during the private beta.
phases.post_beta: Deferred hardening — safe to do after the beta is live and stable.
phases.scale: Only relevant once usage grows beyond the invite cohort.

tasks.title: Real-user performance measurements
tasks.rationale: Synthetic/local checks do not reflect what invitees on real networks and devices experience. We need field data (load, interaction latency) from actual sessions before tuning.
tasks.completion_criteria: A lightweight RUM signal (e.g. navigation + LCP/INP timings) is captured per private app and visible as a distribution in the admin panel, sourced only from consenting beta members with no PII.

tasks.title: Frontend performance budgets & bundle/transfer audit
tasks.rationale: index.html (~520KB) and studio.html (~1.3MB) ship as large single files. Without a transfer budget these will silently regress and hurt first load, especially on mobile.
tasks.completion_criteria: Per-page transfer-size budgets are documented, current sizes measured (gzipped), and a check flags when a page exceeds its budget. Largest offenders have a splitting/compression plan.

tasks.title: Deployment regression comparison
tasks.rationale: Railway auto-deploys from main. A bad deploy can degrade health or performance with no baseline to compare against, making it hard to attribute a regression to a specific deploy.
tasks.completion_criteria: Each deploy records its commit/version plus a snapshot of key health-check durations, so two deploys can be compared and a regression traced to a commit.

tasks.title: Latency & error history
tasks.rationale: The health endpoint is a point-in-time snapshot. Intermittent failures and slow trends are invisible without retained history.
tasks.completion_criteria: Health-check results (status + duration + timestamp) are persisted on a rolling window and the admin panel shows a short trend/history rather than only the latest check.

tasks.title: External AI cost/latency correlation
tasks.rationale: Anthropic spend (Token Usage tab) and request latency are tracked separately. Correlating them reveals which flows are expensive or slow and whether model/config changes help.
tasks.completion_criteria: Per-endpoint AI call latency is recorded alongside token usage so cost and latency can be viewed together per route/flow over time.

tasks.title: Database backup & restore verification
tasks.rationale: Admin SQLite durability depends on the Railway volume (COMMONUNITY_ADMIN_DB_PATH). There is currently no automated backup and no tested restore, so a volume loss would lose invites/members/events.
tasks.completion_criteria: A scheduled backup of the admin SQLite DB exists off the app volume, and a restore has been performed at least once into a scratch environment and verified to reopen cleanly.

tasks.title: Alert ownership
tasks.rationale: Health is only visible when an operator opens /admin. Degraded states (DB unwritable, SMTP down) can go unnoticed. Alerts need a defined owner and channel.
tasks.completion_criteria: Degraded health states trigger a notification to a named owner via a defined channel, with an escalation note documented in the repo.
